A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same DeltaBench study. All 27 pages in each version, including Appendices A–C, support reliable comparison of the text, figures, tables, and equations.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of PRMs and critic models on DeltaBench, alongside empirical reasoning analyses in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and analyses and reports results for two additional critic models in Table 2.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction and PRM/critic evaluation procedures are retained. The corrected Strategy Shift description matches the new-strategy criterion already illustrated in v1 Figure 4; it does not establish a changed annotation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,236-sample DeltaBench covering Math, Programming, PCB, and General Reasoning. The source datasets and category coverage in Appendices A.1 and A.7 are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Doubao-1.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-Max as evaluated critic models. Its original six PRM rows and fifteen critic-model rows are retained, making this a limited expansion of the comparison set.

E3.justification: Sampling, preprocessing, section segmentation, macro-F1 evaluation, the PRM cutoff t = mean minus standard deviation, and HitRate@k settings are unchanged. Appendix A.8 also retains the alternative 5% quantile threshold; no different protocol is reported for the added critics.

E4.justification: The reasoning, reflection, context-length, error-type, first-error ranking, and self-critique analyses are retained, as are the appendix metric comparisons and failure analyses. The new HitRate summary box restates an existing analysis.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged. Figure 10 retains its shaded bands, and v3 adds no run counts, seed information, uncertainty-estimation explanations, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds overall and domain-specific results for Doubao-1.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-Max, with overall F1 scores of 35.25 and 30.49, respectively. Existing numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged, including GPT-4-turbo-128k's leading overall F1 of 40.76.

T1.justification: The PRM threshold definition and Equation (1), HitRate@k = |Sk intersect E| / min(k, |E|), are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and central claims about DeltaBench, reasoning redundancy, limited error detection, and weak self-critique. The added model results do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of context-length degradation, reflection effectiveness, reasoning efficiency, and self-critique remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning annotation costs, subjective bias, and a static benchmark.

D1.justification: Section 2 corrects Strategy Shift's misleading duplication of Reasoning Usefulness and explicitly documents annotating the step where a new strategy begins. This refines the annotation documentation; reannotation is not established. Appendix implementation details and dataset access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Doubao Team (2025) reference alongside the newly evaluated Doubao model. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to reasoning, PRM, and critique research otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits include adding Zhicheng Zheng to the author list, standardizing CoT capitalization, correcting the Strategy Shift description, and removing a redundant Appendix A.2 self-reference and an unresolved citation marker. Most prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Future Life Lab branding, extends Table 2 with two rows, reformats Table 6, and adds a HitRate Key Finding box. Figure sizing and page spacing receive limited adjustments; all sixteen numbered figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves a misleading annotation description and makes Table 2 more useful by placing two additional critics within the existing comparison. These provide limited gains in technical clarity and empirical usefulness. The benchmark design, existing results, analyses, and methodological limitations remain essentially unchanged.
